Growing degree-day methods

Source: vignettes/gdd-methods.Rmd
gdd-methods.Rmd

One framework for all daily methods

For an idealised diurnal profile between TminT_{min} and TmaxT_{max}, define

  • the excess I(x)=1P∫0Pmax⁡(0,T(t)−x)dtI(x) = \frac{1}{P}\int_0^P \max(0, T(t) - x)\,dt, and
  • the exceedance F(x)F(x), the fraction of the day with T(t)>xT(t) > x.

Both depend only on the distribution of temperatures within the day. For a sine wave with mean MM and amplitude AA, with θ=arcsin⁡((x−M)/A)\theta = \arcsin((x - M)/A),

I(x)=1π[(M−x)(π2−θ)+Acosθ],F(x)=12−θπ, I(x) = \frac{1}{\pi}\left[(M - x)\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) + A\cos\theta\right], \qquad F(x) = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{\theta}{\pi},

which is the Baskerville-Emin (1969) formula. For a symmetric triangle I(x)=(Tmax−x)2/(2(Tmax−Tmin))I(x) = (T_{max} - x)^2 / (2(T_{max} - T_{min})) when Tmin<x<TmaxT_{min} < x < T_{max}.

With a lower threshold LL and an upper threshold UU:

Cutoff Degree-days Development above UU
none I(L)I(L) unbounded
horizontal I(L)−I(U)I(L) - I(U) constant at U−LU - L
vertical I(L)−I(U)−(U−L)F(U)I(L) - I(U) - (U - L)F(U) zero
intermediate I(L)−2I(U)+I(2U−L)I(L) - 2I(U) + I(2U - L) decreases with slope -1

Double methods split the day into a rising half (Tmin,d→Tmax,dT_{min,d} \to T_{max,d}) and a falling half (Tmax,d→Tmin,d+1T_{max,d} \to T_{min,d+1}), each contributing half a day.

Methods compared 

tmin <- 8; tmax <- seq(10, 40, by = 1)
methods <- c("average", "single_sine", "single_triangle")
gdd <- sapply(methods, function(m) degree_days(rep(tmin, length(tmax)), tmax,
                                               method = m, base = 10))
matplot(tmax, gdd, type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
        col = c("grey40", "#0B5563", "#E8702A"),
        xlab = "Tmax (degC), Tmin = 8 degC", ylab = "GDD base 10 (degC day)")
legend("topleft", legend = methods, lty = 1, lwd = 2, bty = "n",
       col = c("grey40", "#0B5563", "#E8702A"))

When Tmin<Tb<TmaxT_{min} < T_b < T_{max} the averaging method underestimates heat accumulation because it ignores the warm hours (a consequence of Jensen’s inequality for the convex function max⁡(0,T−Tb)\max(0, T - T_b)).

Cutoffs are not interchangeable 

tmax <- seq(20, 45, by = 1)
cuts <- c("horizontal", "intermediate", "vertical")
gdd <- sapply(cuts, function(k) degree_days(rep(15, length(tmax)), tmax,
                                            base = 10, upper = 30, cutoff = k))
matplot(tmax, gdd, type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
        col = c("#0B5563", "#5DA9C9", "#E8702A"),
        xlab = "Tmax (degC), Tmin = 15 degC",
        ylab = "GDD (degC day), base 10, upper 30")
legend("topleft", legend = cuts, lty = 1, lwd = 2, bty = "n",
       col = c("#0B5563", "#5DA9C9", "#E8702A"))

Hourly data

With hourly observations use degree_hours(); the conversion to degree-days divides the daily sum by 24:

temp <- 12 + 9 * sin(2 * pi * (0:47 - 9) / 24)
degree_hours(temp, base = 10, by_day = TRUE)
#> [1] 3.931741 3.931741

References

Baskerville & Emin (1969); Lindsey & Newman (1956); Sevacherian et al. (1977); Allen (1976); Zalom et al. (1983); McMaster & Wilhelm (1997). Full citations are in ?degree_days.
